description:
FILED s451z, seen while closing #711.  PRE-EXISTING; cosmetic-looking but it
is a WRITE that did not happen.

    use File::Temp qw(tempfile);
    my (undef, $f) = tempfile(OPEN => 0);

        PCL prints on stderr:  warning: Cannot modify non-boxed value in s///

The s/// runtime declines to write back when its target is not a box and
announces instead of dying (which is right -- rule 12's effect-only boundary
does not apply here, the value IS consumed).  What is not known is WHICH
s/// in File::Temp it is and what the missed write costs; the visible output
of the probe is correct, so the substitution is either a no-op in this path or
its result is discarded.

NEXT STEP (cheap, and this is the discriminating measurement): run the probe
with the announcement carrying its FILE and LINE -- the announcer already has
the information at the call site -- or bisect by instrumenting a copy of
File/Temp.pm under `use lib`.  Do not guess at the s///; there are 20-odd in
that module.

BAR: the announcement gone for the right reason (the target is boxed), or a
task filed for whatever the real gap is with its own repro.
subject: "warning: Cannot modify non-boxed value in s///" on stderr from a plain File::Temp::tempfile run
